top_choice_rationale: P001 (Mircea Cărtărescu, credited alone) is my first choice. On public knowledge, the Orbitor trilogy (beginning with Blinding) and Solenoid build memory, the body and dream into one large imaginative architecture. That gives a distinctive voice, formal ambition and imaginative depth, and the poetry and essays appear to belong to the same project, so the whole oeuvre is the object of judgment rather than a single peak. The case rests on literary form and sustained quality, not on nationality, fame or the first-round tally. Its central claim, construction across volumes, can be assessed through translation more directly than a prosodic innovation can, though I cannot verify how much Romanian verbal texture survives. Unresolved doubts remain: whether the very long late books extend the project or repeat it, and how thin the translated coverage of the poetry and essays is. I rank P002 (Adonis) second as a serious rival. My opening placement of him reflects evidentiary confidence about Arabic prosody, not a finding of lesser merit. His claim of renewing a poetic language, if confirmed from the originals, would be a first-rank achievement, and the poems rather than the essays would have to carry the citation. P000 (no award) is last because both proposals name a writer with a substantial, distinctive oeuvre. No independent source verification is claimed.
